reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in replacing fixed-slot embeddings with simplex rotary encodings, which allow permutation symmetry without sacrificing agent controllability. Each agent is embedded as a vertex of a regular simplex in a rotary angle space, ensuring all pairwise distances are equal. This avoids the need for learned positional embeddings tied to fixed rosters. Cross-agent interactions are modeled via sparse hub attention, where each agent communicates through a set of learnable hub tokens. This reduces computational complexity from O(P²) to O(P), making it scalable to many agents. The method leverages transformer-based latent video diffusion with flow matching, enabling generative modeling of multi-agent scenes. The approach is validated on synchronized Minecraft trajectories and real-world robotic datasets, showing promise for applications requiring permutation-invariant modeling.
